newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka air force helicopter gunship missing.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka air force helicopter gunship missing.

text.p: A Sri Lankan air force attack helicopter went missing on Wednesday shortly after take off from a military air base in the island's north, military officials said.
A navy official in Colombo said vessels were searching for the Russian-built Mi-24 helicopter gunship, which was believed to have gone down off the coast of northeastern Mullaitivu district.

Mi-24s form part of the air force's attack fleet used in the war against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of this predominantly Sinhalese island.
It was not immediately known if the helicopter had been shot down by the rebels, who control vast areas of the east and northeast.

Other military officials said the missing aircraft was one of two Mi-24s which had taken off from the Palaly air base in the northern Jaffna peninsula around 12.15 p.m. (0615 GMT) on Wednesday and headed south.
They were unsure where the aircraft, which hold four or five crew, were headed.
Sri Lanka's tiny air force has lost six aircraft this year in operations against the rebels.
A Pucara ground attack aircraft on a bombing mission exploded in midair over the northeastern Polonnaruwa district on Saturday after the pilot had ejected safely.

Tamil rebels blew up a Y-12 transport plane at the China Bay air base in eastern Trincomalee in early March while in February an An-32 transport plane crashed taking off from an air base near Colombo, killing three servicemen and wounding 36.
In January, a Kfir fighter jet crashed after the pilot had ejected soon after takeoff from the Katunayake airbase, just north of Colombo.
A Y-12 with four people aboard and an unmanned drone, both on reconnaissance missions over northern waters, went missing the same month.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
